'''Konstantin P. Bryliakov''' (born 1 June 1977; {{Langx|ru|Константи́н Петро́вич Брыляко́в}}) is a Russian [[chemist]] and author of monographs<ref name="KB-2014">{{Cite book |first1=Konstantin |last1=Bryliakov |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rXDSBQAAQBAJ |title=Environmentally Sustainable Catalytic Asymmetric Oxidations |date=2014 |publisher=[[CRC Press]] |isbn=978-1-4665-8859-2}}</ref><ref name="KB-2017">{{Cite book |first1=Evgenii |last1=Talsi |first2=Konstantin |last2=Bryliakov |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=--2fDgAAQBAJ |title=Applications of EPR and NMR Spectroscopy in Homogeneous Catalysis |date=2017 |publisher=[[CRC Press]] |isbn=978-1-4987-4263-4}}</ref> and over 190 research papers,<ref name="ORCID">{{Cite web |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7009-8950 |title=K. P. Bryliakov |website=[[ORCID]] }}</ref><ref name="Sciact">{{Cite web|url=http://sciact.catalysis.ru/ru/public/profile/10 |title=K. P. Bryliakov's profile |website=Sciact |language=ru }}</ref> textbooks, and patents. He is a professor at [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] and [[Novosibirsk State University]]. He is the head of the Laboratory of Selective Oxidation Catalysis at [[N. D. Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry]] of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].

== Biography ==
Bryliakov was born in [[Yoshkar-Ola]], [[Soviet Union|USSR]]. He studied [[chemistry]] at [[Novosibirsk State University]] from 1994 to 1999, after which he joined the Boreskov Institute of Catalysis as a [[PhD student]] and [[Novosibirsk State University]] as a [[teaching assistant]]. He was elected Professor of [[Novosibirsk State University]] in 2018.

=== Academic career ===
Bryliakov received a Cand. Chem. Sci. ([[Ph.D.|PhD]]) degree in [[chemical physics]] from the [[Voevodsky Institute of Chemical Kinetics and Combustion]], [[Novosibirsk]], in 2001, and a Doctor of Chemical Sciences degree ([[Habilitation]]) in [[catalysis]] from the [[Boreskov Institute of Catalysis]], Novosibirsk, in 2008. Until 2023 he was a head of Department of Mechanisms of Catalytic Reactions at the Boreskov Institute of Catalysis, after which time he joined [[N. D. Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry]]. In 2016, Konstantin Bryliakov was elected professor of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].

Bryliakov served as an invited editor of catalysis journals ''Topics in Catalysis''<ref name="TC-201308">{{Cite journal |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/11244/56/11/page/1 |title=Topics in Catalysis Special Issue: Mechanisms of Catalytic Reactions |journal=Topics in Catalysis |editor-first1=Konstantin P. |editor-last1=Bryliakov |editor-first2=Vasily V. |editor-last2=Kaichev |editor-first3=Valentin N. |editor-last3=Parmon |volume=56 |issue=11 |date=August 2013 |issn=1572-9028 |publisher=[[SpringerLink]] }}</ref> and ''Catalysis Today''.<ref name="CT-">{{Cite journal |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/catalysis-today/vol/279/part/P1 |title=Catalysis Today Special Issue: EuropaCat XII: Catalysis for Chemical Synthesis |editor-first1=Konstantin P. |editor-last1=Bryliakov |editor-first2=Ekaterina S. |editor-last2=Lokteva |journal=Catalysis Today |publisher=[[ScienceDirect]] |issn=0920-5861 |date=1 January 2017 |volume=279 |issue=Part 1 }}</ref> He was also a member of scientific committees of international catalysis conferences.<ref name="BIC-IXICMCR">{{cite web |title=Boreskov Institute of Catalysis{{Snd}} IX International Conference === Research ===
Bryliakov's research interests include [[Green chemistry|green]] [[Enantioselective synthesis|enantioselective (stereoselective) synthesis]] (mainly [[Redox|oxidation]]), [[Biomimetic synthesis|biomimetic chemistry]], [[coordination polymerization]] of olefins, including [[Reaction mechanism|mechanisms of these reactions]]. Konstantin Bryliakov pioneered the use of [[Homochirality|homochiral]] [[Metal–organic framework|metal-organic frameworks]] as [[chiral stationary phase]]s for [[chromatographic separation]] of [[enantiomer]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Nuzhdin, A. L. |author2=Dybtsev, D. N. |author3=Bryliakov, K. P. |author4=Talsi, E. P. |author5=Fedin, V. P. |title= Enantioselective Chromatographic Resolution and One-Pot Synthesis of Enantiomerically Pure Sulfoxides over a Homochiral Zn−Organic Framework |journal=[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]] |issn=1520-5126 |date=2007 |volume=129 |issue=43 |pages=12958–59 |doi=10.1021/ja076276p |pmid=17924635 |url=https://figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/2977744 |language=English |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He discovered a new dynamic [[Non-linear effects|non-linear effect]] in [[asymmetric catalysis]], named asymmetric autoamplification, and proposed the novel, non-autocatalytic chemical model of perbiotic chirality amplification.<ref name="CCC-20170707">{{cite journal |author1=Talsi, E. P. |author2=Bryliakova, A. A. |author3=Rybalova, T. V. |last4=Ottenbacher, R. V. |last5=Bryliakov, K. P. |date=November 4, 2019 |title=Chiral Autoamplification Meets Dynamic Chirality Control to Suggest Nonautocatalytic Chemical Model of Prebiotic Chirality Amplification |journal=Research |language=English |publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science|AAAS]] |volume=2019 |issue= |article-number=4756025 |doi=10.34133/2019/4756025 |pmid=31922134 |issn=2639-5274 |s2cid=99108191|pmc=6946252 }}</ref> Konstantin Bryliakov developed a variety of ''[[Biomimetics|biomimetic]]'' approaches to molecular editing of complex organic molecules via direct selective activation and heterofunctionalization of aliphatic C-H groups.<ref name="CCC-20180621">{{cite journal |author1=Bryliakov, K. P. |date=January 3, 2025 |title=Adding new dimension to non-directed C(sp3)–H functionalizations |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11426-024-2431-3 |journal=Science China Chemistry |language=English |publisher=[[Springer Nature]] |volume= |issue= |pages= |doi=10.1007/s11426-024-2431-3 |issn=1674-7291 |s2cid=103402006|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== International activities ===
Bryliakov has worked at the [[University of Konstanz]], [[University of East Anglia]], [[Reims University]], [[University of Castilla–La Mancha|University of Castilla-La Mancha]], Institute of Chemistry of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and managed several international research projects supported by [[Russian Foundation for Basic Research|RFBR]]. Winner of the President of Chinese Academy of Sciences International Fellowship Award for 2020.
